events.title: Nimrod, son of Cush, becomes a mighty hunter
events.narrative_summary: Cush fathers Nimrod, who begins to be a mighty man on the earth. He is a mighty hunter before the LORD, which gives rise to a proverb.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No date in the text ('he began to be a mighty one on the earth'). Placed by estimate 60 years after the Flood began (anchor.flood), margin 40 years, after Noah's grandsons' generation and before the division of the earth in Peleg's days (about 101 years after the Flood in the MT chain). MACRO_ERA because the text gives no year, only the rise of a figure in the early post-Flood world.

events.title: Nimrod's kingdom begins in Babel, Erech, Akkad and Calneh
events.narrative_summary: The beginning of Nimrod's kingdom is Babel, Erech, Accad and Calneh in the land of Shinar.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'The beginning of his kingdom' follows his rise as a mighty man; 10 years after its start (margin 15 years) is an estimate with no textual date. MACRO_ERA. Babel here is the city; the Tower of Babel story of Gen 11 is not dated by this event.

events.title: Asshur goes out from that land and builds Nineveh and other cities
events.narrative_summary: From that land Asshur went out and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah and Resen between Nineveh and Calah, which is the great city.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'From that land' (10:11) places it after Nimrod's kingdom in Shinar; 10 years after its start with a 15-year margin is an estimate. MACRO_ERA. Reading note: the Hebrew can mean Asshur (the person) went out, or that Nimrod went out to Assyria (so Targum Pseudo-Jonathan and KJV margin); I follow the plain reading of Asshur as subject, as Onkelos does. Travel times are not computed: the text gives no journey, only building (Accad to Nineveh is about 388 km straight line).

events.title: The Canaanite clans scatter across their territory
events.narrative_summary: After the Canaanite clans were born, they were spread abroad, and the Canaanite border ran from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim as far as Lasha.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Afterward' (10:18) places the scattering after the births of the Canaanite peoples; not tied by the text to the division of Peleg's days, which I use as a rough anchor: 10 years after its start, margin 30 years, duration 50 years. MACRO_ERA. Territory description in 10:19 is the result, not a separate event. No journey is recorded, so no travel time is used.

events.title: The earth is divided in Peleg's days
events.narrative_summary: In the days of Peleg the earth was divided, and the name Peleg records it.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'In his days' (10:25) with no year. Peleg lived 239 years (Gen 11:16-19), so 'his days' cover his whole life. The start is anchored on his birth with offset 120 years and margin 120 years (0 to 240 years after his birth, covering his full lifespan); the midpoint of 120 years is a convention, not a reading of the text. Duration 10 years is a nominal span. MACRO_ERA because the text sets it only in Peleg's days. Whether this is the Babel dispersal is a reading, not stated.

events.title: Eber's son Peleg is born
events.narrative_summary: To Eber two sons are born; one is named Peleg, the other Joktan. Peleg is so named because in his days the earth was divided.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Not dated in this chapter. By the MT chain of Gen 11:10-16 from the Flood: Arpachshad 2 years after, Shelah 35 years after Arpachshad's birth, Eber 30 after Shelah, Peleg 34 after Eber: 2+35+30+34 = 101 years after the Flood began. Offset 101 years from anchor.flood, margin 3 years (age counted in whole years), REGNAL_YEAR since the date comes from numbered ages.
